conventions.convention: Empirical covariance blocks use divisor N, with N ≥ 2; observation perturbations are independent across members and independent of the forecast ensemble and forecast errors.

The EnKF limit fixes observation data and a finite horizon before N tends to infinity; initialization and per-member perturbations have the model laws and are independent across members and times and of initialization. Observation covariances are positive definite; state and process covariances may be singular.
Joint exchangeability means invariance of the entire paired row under a common permutation, rather than separate exchangeability of its components.
3DVAR requires positive-definite background and observation covariances and returns an analysis point, with no analysis covariance output.
4DVAR uses compatible open decision domains and continuously differentiable maps; its gradient call has a finite update limit and reports domain failure without promising a minimizer.

Filtering and smoothing are conditional-kernel versions that may differ on null observation histories; conditional existence is imported under the cited standard-Borel model hypotheses and inherited AC assumption.
The tracking contraction is measured in the stated state norm, while observation errors use the Euclidean norm; κ is the sum of the state norms of the columns of K.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated finite-horizon linear-Gaussian EnKF with positive-definite observation covariances, analysis-member moments and gain operator-norm moments of every finite order p ≥ 1 are bounded uniformly in ensemble size and member index at each applicable time.

Under AC, fixed observations, positive-definite observation covariances, iid model-prior initialization and the stated independent Gaussian perturbations, the deterministic-Kalman-gain reference analysis members are iid with law N(m_{k|k}, P_{k|k}) at every k ≤ T.

For jointly exchangeable paired rows in a fixed finite dimension, if the reference members are iid with a fixed finite-fourth-moment law and the first paired difference tends to zero in L4, the empirical mean and divisor-N covariance converge in probability, entry by entry, to the reference mean and covariance.
Let 1 ≤ q < s < ∞. If finite-dimensional random vectors Z_n converge to Z in probability, E||Z||^s is finite and sup_n E||Z_n||^s is finite, then E||Z_n − Z||^q tends to zero.

If the forecast states, forecast errors, observation perturbations, and any reference-member variables form an exchangeable input row, then the updated states together with those reference variables are exchangeable.

For jointly exchangeable real paired rows, if reference members are pairwise uncorrelated with a common fixed square-integrable law and the first paired difference tends to zero in L2, the empirical X mean converges in L2, hence in probability, to the reference expectation.

For the stated positive-definite B and Γ, the 3DVAR analysis is the unique global minimizer of J. Under the stated Gaussian forecast and independent Gaussian observation-error model, it is the unique posterior-density MAP point and the exact one-step Kalman mean update with identity transition and zero process covariance.

published_dependencies.used_for: Cauchy–Schwarz, product-moment bounds and comparison of probability-space Lp norms.
Measurable finite-dimensional forecast and observation maps.
Explicit inherited choice assumptions in Gaussian constructions and conditional-law suppliers.
Gaussian vectors with possibly singular covariance, their affine realizations, means and covariances.
Existence and uniqueness of positive-diagonal Cholesky factors for positive-definite innovation matrices and weighted least-squares factors.
Finite-horizon model dimensions, independent Gaussian noises and positive-semidefinite covariance conventions.
Joint Gaussianity of independent reference-member state and noise stacks.
Positive Gaussian densities and the elementary finite-moment argument.
Eigenvalue bounds controlling inverse innovation operator norms.
Vanishing centered cross terms in iid reference empirical-average variance calculations.
Converting expected coupling errors and iid-average variance bounds into convergence in probability.
Posterior densities from jointly measurable Gaussian likelihoods with positive finite marginal normalizers.
Gaussian prior and likelihood density formulas in the 3DVAR MAP theorem and nonlinear-observation example.
Existence and uniqueness of the 3DVAR minimizer through an injective weighted least-squares map and its normal equation.

concerns.concern: F1 inaccurately restates the supplier: “if exchangeable rows are pairwise uncorrelated and are close in L2 to a common row, their empirical means converge in L2.” The cited lemma requires joint exchangeability of paired rows, pairwise uncorrelated reference variables U_{N,i}, a fixed square-integrable reference law, and L2 convergence of the paired difference. It does not require the X variables to be pairwise uncorrelated. The proof's actual applications satisfy the correct supplier hypotheses, so the issue is the wording of F1.

seams_checked.note: The 4DVAR call supplies a C1 objective on an open domain, a valid initial point, finite update limit and supported step parameters. The gradient supplier's stopping predicate implements the limit and its fixed-step branch reports domain failure. Neither page imports a general nonconvex optimizer-convergence claim; the Armijo termination argument supports finite backtracking.

The assimilation definition imports full-history conditional-kernel smoothing terminology and preserves null-history version freedom. Its separate existence citation is conditional on the standard-Borel model hypotheses. The assimilation page's RTS caveat matches the supplier algorithm and theorem: every inverted forecast covariance must be positive definite, with no pseudoinverse extension asserted.
